x: The Walk went to the rapidly improving Charlie Churcher, with Rutland once again second, and Snell in third position. Altogether a fine evening's sport and one especially noteworthy and outstanding for our Juniors.

Don Brown walked amazingly well to win the Walk from 20 yards in 14 min. 10 sec., without anyone to push him over the last 300 yards. Rutland, a fast and fair walker, with several years of his 'teens still to run, was second, not for the first time this season.

The walkers have shown up well in Open competitions, and in Heather and Rutland we have two full of promise for the future, whilst the present is in very good hands.

Rutland, who had an allowance of 8 mins. 30 secs. Rutland, when only 15, won our Novice Track Walk, and now, while still a month or two short of seventeen, showed excellent form to finish 23rd in 60 min. 27 seconds, and annex first prize.

Our two teams had met at Euston, and despite the regrettable indisposition of John Rutland, who had promised to do so well in this race, but at the last minute was unable to travel, we made the journey optimistically, knowing that our first choice would give a good account of themselves at Fort Dunlop later in the day.

In fact, it is rather surprising that we could still take second place, and this is due to some very fine walking by Joe King, sound work by the Bros. Churcher, and good backing by the youthful Rutland.

Rutland can do better than the time he recorded on this occasion. The fifth man, "Doug" Earle, with a 5-min. allowance, carried off the sealed handicap, with Frank Jarvis, who followed him in, and with the same allowance, second.

Of the younger walkers, Jack Rutland and Reg Elson both gave sound performances. Rutland would have done even better if he had not been in the lead early on, and when experience brings more knowledge of even pace, we may expect an outstanding performance from him.
Harry Thaxter did well to finish 12th—our eighth man! Had either Coleman or Rutland been declared as a "B" team man, we should have taken another set of awards, but we must not be too greedy!

A team, unfortunately far from our strongest, competed in the "Leicester Mercury" 20 Miles Walk. Fred Rickards was 4th 2hr. 53min. 20sec.), Rutland 10th (3hr. 1min. 4sec.), Sutton 13th (3hr. 3min. 10sec.), and Doubleday 42nd.

It is interesting to note that Jack Rutland, who finished 4th, was at this stage 12th. At 11 miles, Clayton had increased his lead to 400 yards from Charlie, and McMullen and Pat Sapcote had dropped to 4th, with Wright and Bidgood making up ground.

A team of four supported the South Wales Argus 15½ miles Open promoted by Newport Harriers, and the race provided an opportunity for Messrs. Wright, Rutland and Robbins for a reunion with friends and relatives. There was a good entry with 42 individuals and 4 teams.

Jack Bidgood started going up towards the front quite early with Jack Wakeley and Jack Rutland not too far back. Then there followed all in quick succession the remaining five of the “ A ” Team, Don Heath, Hugh McGreechan, “Sir” Harry Shields, Joe Wilson and Dick Frazer.

Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakeley and Readman, closely followed by Sapcote, Sutton and Robins.
